text.p: IZVESTIA
- People's patience is on the verge of exhaustion, President Boris Yeltsin is quoted as saying during his state of the nation address on Thursday.
- The president has identifief "order" as the main ideological goal for the next year.
- Russia's southern Stavropol region is reinforcing its border with Chechnya with local police and interior ministry troops pulled out from the rebel republic earlier this year.
SEVODNYA

- "Chubais's annual address to the nation" - the paper headlines its report on the president's state of nation speech in the Kremlin. A flood of rumours has it that Chubais, the president's chief-of-staff will join the government.
- Government reshuffle speculation, which has been feeding mass media for the last week, have been put on hold for uncertain period of time.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia will breathe easy if the ideals of President's address to the nation are implemented.
- Changes have not yet taken place but Chubias's new appointment to the government has nearly been confirmed.
- Boris Yeltsin has declared war on the bureaucracy.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- Order will be restored in the the country, headlines the paper over the full text of Yeltsin's annual address.
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIYA
- The president's address is more reminiscent of the words of a children's song - "Tomorrow, tomorrow, not today..".
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The president has promised to separate the state from crime, writes the paper referring to Yeltsin's key call to root out corruption and crime from the government structures.
- Generally Yeltsin's speech sounded like "a new song about old problems", says the paper.
- About 50,000 children under 18 are registered as abandoned and are running wild in the capital.
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
